comment: * The Java representation of the HTML5 PostMessage event. See * * https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/comms.html#the-messageevent-interfaces * for definition of a MessageEvent in HTML5.

variables.name: TYPE_STRING
variables.comment: * Indicates the payload of WebMessageCompat is String.

variables.name: TYPE_ARRAY_BUFFER
variables.comment: * Indicates the payload of WebMessageCompat is JavaScript ArrayBuffer.

methods.name: public int getType()
methods.comment:
* Returns the payload type of the message.
     *
     * @return the payload type of WebMessageCompat.

methods.name: public byte @NonNull [] getArrayBuffer()
methods.comment:
* Returns the ArrayBuffer data of message. A ArrayBuffer or Transferable ArrayBuffer can be * received from JavaScript. This should only be called when {@link #getType()} returns * {@link #TYPE_ARRAY_BUFFER}. Example: * 
     * WebMessageCompat message = ... // The WebMessageCompat received or prepared.
     * if (message.getType() == WebMessageCompat.TYPE_ARRAY_BUFFER) {
     *     byte[] arrayBuffer = message.getArrayBuffer();
     *     // Access arrayBuffer data here.
     * }
     *
* * @return ArrayBuffer payload data.

methods.name: public String getData()
public WebMessagePortCompat @Nullable [] getPorts()
methods.comment:
* Returns the ports that are sent with the message, or {@code null} if no port
     * is sent.
